transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: ~41 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus O'Neill (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (CTO - BlueCove), Priya Kapoor (Platform Eng - BlueCove), Aisha Morgan (Head MLOps - BlueCove)

Summary: quick weekly POC check-in focused on rollout / go-live planning. Covered canary strategy, cutover windows, monitoring/runbooks, rollback criteria, and next steps to get a staging canary scheduled. Some brief security questions re: KMS and audit logs.

Topics:
- Canary vs A/B and cutover approaches
- Monitoring, alerts, and runbooks
- Performance targets and SLOs (p99 latency, throughput)
- Data residency and KMS for private deployment
- Next-step tasks and timeline

Transcript:
[10:30:05] Lara Chen: All right, good morning everyone, thanks for making time. This is the weekly POC sync. Today we'll focus on rollout planning canary strategy, cutover, monitoring and runbooks. Marcus is here for the technical details.
[10:30:22] Daniel Reyes: Morning. We're hoping to have a plan to present to ops next week, so I'd like specifics on the canary and rollback, and an estimate for how long the cutover will take.
[10:30:35] Marcus O'Neill: Yep, I can walk through what we've been testing in staging and suggested thresholds. Quick note: our staging measurements used a 5k rps mimic and we saw tail latencies around 220ms at p95, p99 closer to 780ms but that included some unoptimized kv-cache settings.
[10:31:05] Priya Kapoor: sorry, can you say kv-cache again?
[10:31:10] Marcus O'Neill: kv-cache, like the transformer KV cache, we had aggressive TTLs in staging, which impacted cold starts, so the p99 spiked. With prefix caching and warmed instances that drops a lot.
[10:31:38] Aisha Morgan: got it. For the canary, we're planning something like 5% of traffic for 24h then 25% for 12h then full? We're still flexible.
[10:31:50] Lara Chen: That's a reasonable pattern. For customers in your situation we typically recommend a two-phase canary: first functional canary at low traffic to validate correctness and logs, then an increasing traffic canary to validate latency/cost under load. We can provide an automated canary runbook for that.
[10:32:12] Daniel Reyes: Functional checks what are those? Just correctness and sampling outputs? Also we need to ensure redwood's fallback behavior is clear if capacity hits the dedicated pool limit.
[10:32:26] Marcus O'Neill: Functional checks usually include a set of smoke prompts and evaluation heuristics make sure the model responses meet thresholds for hallucination rate and token usage. We'll include sampling and a small evaluation harness. For fallback, the routing policy can send overflow to a cheaper variant or back to hosted but we'll need to align on what BlueCove wants for fail-open vs fail-closed.
[10:33:05] Priya Kapoor: we definitely prefer fail-open for non-sensitive routes and fail-closed for PHI-related endpoints. Also we need to ensure KMS integration for encryption at rest is Redwood Private supporting our HSM?
[10:33:20] Lara Chen: Yes, the Private deployment supports KMS/HSM integrations; we have a guide and SOC2 doc. I'll attach the onboarding KMS checklist.
[10:33:38] Aisha Morgan: quick question on monitoring: what out-of-the-box dashboards do you provide and what do we need to add to our Prometheus?
[10:33:48] Marcus O'Neill: Redwood Console provides per-route latency breakdowns, token-level cost, error rates, and tracing hooks. For Prometheus we can emit metrics via exporter: request_count, p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and queue_depth for the runtime. We'll share the metrics mapping.
[10:34:18] Daniel Reyes: and alerting thresholds? we want to codify the rollback criteria.
[10:34:24] Lara Chen: Typical rollback criteria we recommend: sustained p99 > 1s for >5 minutes, error rate increase >2x baseline, and any data-exfiltration or security failure. Those are customizable.
[10:34:40] Priya Kapoor: for our SLA we need an SLO doc: target p95 < 500ms and p99 < 900ms for 75% of endpoints, with per-route exceptions. We'll send a list.
[10:34:55] Marcus O'Neill: that aligns with staging numbers; with batching/quantization suggestions we can likely hit that. For HQ traffic we recommend dedicated pooling with auto-scale burst to handle peak windows.
[10:35:15] Daniel Reyes: timeline if we start canary 2026-06-02 in staging with your SE assistance, how quickly can we go to full?
[10:35:24] Marcus O'Neill: depends on canary results. If functional and latency look good at 25% over 12-24h, I'd say a phased cutover to 100% over the next 48h is feasible. We want to leave a rollback window of at least 1 hour during which we can redirect traffic back to previous endpoint.
[10:35:45] Aisha Morgan: what about data residency and logs retention for audit? We need 7 years of audit logs for certain flows.
[10:35:55] Lara Chen: We can configure log retention in Private deployments and integrate with your SIEM. We also have audit-log exports for dedicated customers. I'll attach the audit-log export doc.
[10:36:10] Daniel Reyes: ok good. Pricing do you have an estimate for the dedicated burst capacity we discussed?
[10:36:18] Lara Chen: I'll send pilot pricing options baseline reserved plus burst buffer pricing and a per-token delta for high throughput. Expect that in the canary runbook bundle.
[10:36:30] Priya Kapoor: we noticed earlier the tokenizer differences caused cost variance in staging, any mitigation?
[10:36:36] Marcus O'Neill: yes tokenization can vary by model; we'll recommend model/quantization pairs and grouping routes to optimize token usage. Also prefix caching reduces repeated tokenization costs.
[10:36:55] Daniel Reyes: any security signoffs required from Redwood before go-live?
[10:37:00] Lara Chen: we'll need to confirm SOC2 scope for this pilot and SAML SSO details for your org, plus the KMS key policy. I'll have our security packet and SSO setup guide in the email.
[10:37:18] Aisha Morgan: can you also include the runbook template with exact CLI steps to roll back? We need that for our ops runbook binder.
[10:37:28] Marcus O'Neill: yes, we'll provide a runbook with exact steps: change routing policy, scale down dedicated pool, revert model pin. We'll include the CLI snippets and console screenshots.
[10:37:45] Lara Chen: Great. Before we wrap, let's be explicit about next steps and owners. I'll send: canary runbook + pricing, security docs, and runbook template. Marcus will schedule the staging canary for 6/2 and run the first load test. Priya will send infra diagram.
[10:38:05] Daniel Reyes: perfect. Any other questions?
[10:38:12] Priya Kapoor: just confirm the cutover window length you suggested a phased 48h to full, with one-hour rollback windows?
[10:38:22] Marcus O'Neill: correct phased rollout: 5% x24h, 25% x12h, 100% ramp over 48h, with defined rollback triggers and one-hour manual rollback hold. We'll document exact steps.
[10:38:40] Lara Chen: ok I'll capture all in the email and add links to the docs: runbook (link), KMS checklist (link), SOC2 packet (link), metrics mapping (link).
[10:38:55] Daniel Reyes: thanks everyone.
[10:39:00] Lara Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts today.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: runbook (link to internal doc), SOC2 packet (link), KMS checklist (link), metrics mapping exporter (link), pilot pricing spreadsheet (link). Some names/terms may be imperfectly transcribed (kv-cache was heard as k v cache a couple times).
